event.active_blue_south_blue_01_brass_ba: You recover the case before it fills with water. The tuba returns dented but playable.
The band finally accepts that one instrument is not worth a second rescue.
You throw empty boxes overboard and find a dry place for the tuba.
During the transfer, a tuba case slips between the hulls. Three musicians want to go back for it while the ferry starts spinning again.
You send their position toward the coast and keep your deck clear.
You take the performers aboard and leave their cases tarped on the ferry.
You tow the entire ferry slowly while the brass section never stops playing.
A ferry of musicians drifts with its engine dead, brass instruments still raised. They are due in Samba City tonight and are already arguing whether instruments or passengers board first.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_briss_cr: The crate bursts on the stones, but the lane is empty.
Let it drop
The dockers take the weight together and set it down without further damage.
Lower it by hand
You lighten the crate in place; its cargo can be moved in smaller loads.
Open the crate
The backup line holds, but the crate is still hanging at head height. The crane cannot lift it and the dock has to reopen.
The Hanging Crate
The upright kicks you back hard and the crate drops a meter.
The gantry stops moving before the load touches the dock.
You slow the movement, but a beam splits under the strain.
You brace the gantry long enough for dockers to regain the cable.
Brace the gantry
The cable lashes the dock and cuts your forearm.
You freeze the load before it swings across the dock lane.
You catch the guide, but the crate slams into a stack of barrels.
You recover the guide and stop the crate from building momentum.
Grab the guide rope
You push bystanders back and let the crate fall into an empty patch.
Clear the dock
At Briss Port, a crane cable snaps over a busy lane. A suspended crate starts sweeping across the dock while workers scramble for a second guide.
Snapped Cable
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_centaure: Your tone hardens the office and the merchants lose their last chance to appeal.
The office suspends the entire hold until the records are checked.
The supervisor hears you without reopening the gates.
You get ten minutes to compare both ledgers.
You leave the office and let merchants settle the mismatch without you.
You blame the wrong column and get two innocent cargoes blocked.
You prove the error before guards shut down the whole dock.
You find the mismatch, but too late to save the day’s sale.
You trace the mismatch to one line copied twice.
In a South Blue city port, the royal office and dockworkers show two different totals for the same cargo. Guards are already closing the gates as merchants protest.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_cold_por: You win a damaged lot nobody wanted to load in the snow.
You help sellers cover the lots before the next gust.
You spot the crates that took water before freezing and avoid a bad purchase.
You leave the auction to the cold and walk away without cargo.
In a cold South Blue market square, crates from warmer ports are being sold before frost damages them further. Buyers are already tapping boards to listen for frozen water inside.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_crosscur: A long line is enough for them to reform.
Leave a stout line
The lane is clear; you leave the fishers to reset their nets.
Move on
You tow the skiff out of traffic into calm water.
Take a skiff in tow
One skiff keeps spinning in the current. Its skipper shouts that he only needs a solid pull to get out of traffic.
The Last Skiff
The knife slips: you cut your palm and the net stays caught.
You even recover the line and toss it back to the fishers.
You free the hull late and lose a few planks.
The net drops cleanly before it tears at the rudder.
Cut the outer net
You stop dead. The fishers clear the lane themselves, but the convoy loses its lead.
Heave to
Your wake rolls a skiff and its cargo spills overboard.
You guide the whole group clear without losing a crate.
You avoid the collision, but the nets rake the hull.
You open a clean lane through the lines.
Thread between the skiffs
Three fishing skiffs drift across a merchant current. Their nets are already catching your hull while another ship closes from behind: the lane has to open now.
Nets Across the Lane
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_drifting: You cut loose the worst-positioned barge to keep the others out of the current.
Sacrifice one barge
You focus on the harvest; the barges will have to be recovered later.
Save the baskets
You accept the delay and tow the barges toward a safer lane.
Tow the whole train
A towline snaps as soon as you gather the barges. The full train is too heavy to hold course; you have to choose what you save.
The Impossible Tow
You come in too fast: the bow crushes baskets on the first barge.
You recover the lead barge and line the others up behind it.
You catch the barge, but the impact damages your side.
You take the barge in tow before it drifts offshore.
Catch the lead barge
You miss the rail and fall hard between the hulls.
You cross barge to barge and secure the whole train.
You get the line on, but split your knee on a crate.
The towline bites in the right place and stops the drift.
Jump with a towline
You note heading and speed, then signal the barges to the next crew you meet.
Mark their drift
A train of farm barges has lost its tug in the chop. Baskets of vegetables roll across the decks while the current pulls them offshore.
Harvest Adrift
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_forest_m: You refuse medicine you do not need and leave the stock for the village.
You pay for the preparation and let the clinic keep its supplies.
You help sort leaves and leave with advice instead of a debt.
In a South Blue forest village, a clinic lacks hands more than leaves. The herbalist offers travelers a simple exchange: one hour sorting herbs for one preparation.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_harbor_n: You spend the evening filling basins and free the staff to treat patients.
You leave the staff to work without adding one more body to the corridor.
You pay a runner to fetch clean linen and save the clinic time.
You help separate emergencies from injuries that can wait.
In a South Blue port, the clinic receives injured dockers and two feverish sailors at once. What the staff lacks most is hands to move water, linen, and patients.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_icewake_: You leave the area before another slab breaks loose.
Get clear fast
You mark the water’s motion before it vanishes under the ice.
Mark the counter-current
Your signal turns the following vessel away before the gap fully closes.
Warn the ship astern
Beyond the first floe, the water suddenly reverses. A merchant ship is already following your wake, unaware the opening is about to close.
The Blue Gap
You refuse the lane and take the longer route toward clearer water.
Back away from the ice
The rudder slips and the bow bites the ice.
You use the ice itself to turn without losing speed.
You make it through, but a floe scrapes the hull for several seconds.
The ship swings through just before the lane closes.
Force the turn
You mistake a shadow for a lane: the hull hits a submerged slab.
You also spot the counter-current that will close the lane behind you.
You find the opening, but too late to avoid a side impact.
The real lane appears between two floes.
Read the blue water
A cold South Blue current carries floes into the merchant route. Ahead, the opening is closing faster than expected and the hull has no room to spare.
Icewake
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_jewel_wh: Eight months later, a dispatch tells you the caravan changed its ropes and shelters after the squall.
Read the dispatch
You send back what you remember about where visibility broke down.
Send your notes
Eight months after the whiteout, a courier from South Blue’s cold routes finds you. The guides want to confirm what they changed after the accident.
Dispatch from the Cold
The guides send a small fee for helping shape their new procedures.
Accept their fee
You refuse to put your name on a shelter maintained by others.
Decline the plaque
Sixteen months after the accident, a new shelter opens on the route. The guides want to settle your part in the story before the next winter.
The Next Shelter
You build a low snow wall and wait for the whiteout to lift before moving.
Build a snow wall
You slip with the injured traveler and both hit the ice.
You keep enough strength to go back for a second person.
You make progress, but the effort drains you before shelter.
You carry the injured traveler into shelter.
Carry the injured
You lose the rope and walk to the lip of a crevasse before backing away.
You spot a break in the shelf and turn the whole group before it gives way.
You find the group after a long loop that freezes your hands.
You keep the rope at the right angle all the way to shelter.
Follow the rope
On the Jewel Ice Sheet, a squall erases the horizon in seconds. A caravan clings to a guide rope; one traveler has fallen and nobody can see the shelter.
Whiteout
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_karate_o: You arrange another day instead of turning practice into a brawl.
Ask for a rematch
You end the exchange with a clean bow, win or lose.
Bow cleanly
You leave the ring without ceremony. A few looks cool behind you.
Leave without bowing
The ring clears, but everyone is still waiting for your bow. Here, how you end the exchange matters almost as much as the result.
The Last Bow
You drive straight in and hit the floor with the wind knocked out of you.
You control the center without hitting harder than needed.
You stay in the exchange, but take a clean hit to the ribs.
You set your base and force your opponent out of the ring.
Take the center
You watch the bout and learn where fighters lose balance.
Watch a round
You slide out of the ring and twist your ankle.
You win without letting your opponent touch center once.
You dodge the blows but eventually step out yourself.
You rotate the exchange until the other fighter steps out.
Work the edge
On Karate Island, a painted ring outside a training hall stays open to travelers. A local fighter waves you in: one exchange is enough to see how you hold your footing.
Open Mat
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_kutsukku: You note the spacing of the marks and learn to read their improvised shoals.
You give the poles a wide berth and leave the fishers to reset their own markers.
You stand several poles back up and the lane becomes readable again for small coasters.
Near a small South Blue island, fishers mark shoals with long painted poles. The swell has knocked several flat and the markers now point toward the wrong lane.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_lantern_: You keep the last log. South Blue will keep ringing without you.
Keep the last note
You send the notes back with the next ship bound for South Blue.
Send the log back
You left South Blue before the next meeting. A courier hands you the last relay log: local keepers are taking the chain back without you.
The Last Bell
You leave the network to the pilots who actually know the channels.
Let the pilots run it
You push for a shared roster every port can inspect.
Publish the roster
You refuse to become keeper of a coastal system that is not yours.
Walk away
A year after the incident, several South Blue ports finally compare bell logs. The keepers want to know who should be allowed to correct a false signal.
One Winter Later
You have sensitive routes masked from smugglers and cargo hunters.
Hide sensitive routes
The ports keep the roster open despite protests from the most powerful.
Keep names open
The public roster works, but captains have begun copying light schedules to predict the busiest merchant routes.
The Open Roster
The pilots accept one minimum shared code without giving up their local charts.
Set one common rule
Each port keeps its habits; you require only one universal stop signal.
Trust the ports
The private network keeps outsiders away, but two pilot guilds already use incompatible rhythms. One ship receives two different instructions a day apart.
Pilots Among Themselves
You return the logs and leave South Blue to rebuild the network without you.
Leave the chain
You darken the least reliable stretch rather than broadcast false bearings.
Darken one stretch
You help the ports bring enough stations back into agreement to save the season.
Repair the chain
Several years have passed. A storm season has destroyed two stations and isolated a third; the old compromises are no longer enough to keep the chain coherent.
The Broken Chain
You push merchant ports to jointly fund the stations they all use.
Share the cost
You accept a network paid by captains who want maintained signals.
Charge for passage
You refuse a common fund; only stations able to survive on volunteer work will remain.
Keep it voluntary
The network is working again, but maintenance costs more than emergency repairs. The ports now argue over the bill instead of the code.
Who Pays for the Light?
You leave the roster with a stable chain and keepers able to run it without you.
Hand it to locals
The bells remain a shared South Blue service. Your name stays in the earliest corrected logs.
Leave the network open
Years after the first mistake, most ports finally use compatible signals. One choice remains: whether your name should stay attached to the network.
Open Lights
You force a fee low enough for small coasters to keep using the lights.
Cap the fee
You take your share of the proceeds and let the ports handle the criticism.
Take your share
The passage-funded network has become reliable, but small coasters dispute the fees. Your old decision comes back as a bill.
Paid Lights
You sound a simple stop signal; silence is better than a false bearing.
Break the rhythm
You repeat the correct rhythm until nearby ships copy it.
Correct the code
You keep the faulty sequence and exact time: someone will have to explain it later.
Record the mistake
One bell repeats the same wrong bearing despite your signals. The coaster finally stops, but the faulty station keeps guiding other ships.
The Wrong Bell
You anchor until the lanterns finally agree.
Anchor and wait
You overestimate the channel and the hull hits bottom hard.
You cut a line clean enough for two ships behind to copy it.
You make it through without signals, but scrape bottom for several seconds.
You hold a safe line until a reliable light returns.
Navigate dark
You follow the wrong rhythm and skim a shoal before realizing the error.
You also identify which coastal station reversed its code.
You identify the faulty bell after a detour that shakes the hull.
You recover the true sequence among the conflicting signals.
Triangulate the bells
In South Blue fog, three coastal bells give incompatible bearings. A coaster behind you is already following the wrong rhythm toward an unseen shoal.
Bells in the Fog
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_market_b: You buy the lot before the bell and keep it from going back into storage.
You connect the farmer with a passing cook before closing.
You repack the crop properly so it survives until the next market.
The bell rings and the lot goes back to the cart.
At a South Blue farm market, the closing bell is about to ring and one grower still has a full lot unsold. Storage will cost nearly as much as the sale.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_medicine: You give the doctor back the deck and keep your course.
Give the deck back
You keep one fragile crate sheltered until the next dock.
Keep one crate dry
You help stabilize the deckhand who split his forehead on the rail.
Treat their deckhand
Once the transfer is done, a medical-boat deckhand collapses: he stayed upright only to protect the crates. The doctor still needs another pair of hands.
The Last Patient
You cut too close to a shoal and the escort takes a hard hit.
You save enough time for the doctor to treat an injured passenger underway.
You keep the medical boat moving, at the cost of a collision with your hull.
You give it a stable route to the next harbor.
Clear the route
You copy their signal and pass it to ships you meet; the route opens slowly.
Relay the flag
A crate breaks between the hulls and injures your ankle.
You organize the transfer fast enough for the medical boat to depart light.
You save most of the crates, but two go overboard.
The medicine crosses safely onto your deck.
Transfer the crates
A small South Blue medical boat raises a white flag between swells. Its rudder is failing and its crates must reach port before the bandages get soaked.
Medical Flag
A courier from Baterilla hands you a note: the medical boat delivered most of its cargo.
Accept their thanks
You send the reward back to the clinic. Your name starts circulating among medical crews.
Send the money back
Six months later, a courier finds you with the medical boat’s receipt. The clinic wants to settle what it now considers a debt to you.
The Baterilla Receipt
You refuse to turn it into a lasting debt. The story ends on a clean salute.
Close the account
The courier gives you the latest habits of South Blue medical boats; you know better where to look for help.
Take the route notes
A second message arrives: the clinic turned your help into a habit and now passes your name among its visiting captains.
One Route Stays Open
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_mira_emp: {{npc_mira}} accepts a berth and joins your crew.
You spend an hour comparing recent South Blue routes without discussing commitment.
You let {{npc_mira}} look for another deck and keep the relationship intact.
At a South Blue recruitment port, {{npc_mira}} studies departure notices posted by the docks. She recognizes you and asks one simple question: does your next course need a real navigator?
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_port_din: You pay market price for the dinghy and leave with a simple boat.
You find two honest repairs and no reason to rush.
You let the bidding continue without raising a hand.
On a South Blue trade quay, three small dinghies are being sold as-is after inspection. One is clean enough to leave today if someone pays cash.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_redfin_f: The trader offers you a share so the queue forgets the second weighing.
Take his cut
You break the mechanism. The market will have to weigh another way until tomorrow.
Smash the scale
You recover the true standard weight hidden behind a crate and set it on the counter.
Take the real weight
The trader pulls you behind the counter. On a shelf, a true standard weight sits beside an already-open purse.
The Back-Room Weight
You accuse the wrong plate and the whole counter laughs.
You expose the trick before the whole queue without giving the merchant time to hide it.
You sense the fraud but cannot show where it hides.
You spot the hollow weight hidden under the plate.
Spot the false weight
The queue turns on you and two men shove you away from the counter.
The merchant takes his own scale apart before the crowd does it for him.
A few customers listen, but nobody wants to be first to protest.
The queue demands a second weighing for every sack.
Turn the queue
You leave the line and refuse to play with a scale nobody wants checked.
Refuse the price
At Redfin Cove, a trader weighs sacks on a scale that always favors him. The queue knows it, but nobody wants to lose their place or draw his guards.
Redfin Scales
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_redfin_s: Five months later, two Redfin men find you: the trader lost several customers and wants the account settled.
Face the collectors
You refuse the meeting and send one reply: the scale was crooked.
Send a hard reply
Five months after the scale incident, two men tied to the stall find you. The trader considers you responsible for the sales he lost.
Redfin’s Account
You pay to close the account for good.
Buy peace
You spread the trick publicly; the stall’s name travels faster than its collectors.
Spread the story
The trader finally drops it: chasing this story costs him more than the old scale did.
Close it without paying
Seven months later, the dispute returns one last time as an offer: money, silence, or reputation. This time, no scale decides for you.
A Weightless Debt
Your bluff rings false; the skiffs close in, certain they have a target.
They bolt before you finish your fake inspection.
They hesitate without leaving and keep you under watch.
A fake procedure shouted through a speaking trumpet is enough to scatter them.
Bluff a patrol
You cut too deep and scrape bottom before getting out.
You send them around a false lane and vanish behind a headland.
You lose them, but not before striking a shoal.
The skiffs give up when your wake becomes too hard to follow.
Lose them in shoals
You make a clean course change and deny them the excuse for an encounter.
Change route
Two flagless skiffs leave a cove and settle into your wake at a steady distance. They show no weapons, but copy every course change you make.
Redfin Skiffs
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_royal_co: You shorten sail and let them settle their battle of protocol ahead of you.
Both cutters refuse to yield and squeeze you between their wakes.
Your line forces both captains to keep the same distance.
You get through, but one courier clips your side at the last moment.
You hold course and both cutters finally give way.
Your challenge triggers a volley of insults and one cutter crowds your hull.
Both couriers salute before reforming into a clean line.
They ignore you and continue their contest of precedence.
You make their quarrel look ridiculous enough that they slow down.
Two royal cutters converge on the same lane, each demanding priority in its kingdom’s name. Your ship arrives exactly between them as both captains refuse to slow down.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_royal_ta: You make them compare receipts before the cart leaves. Two sacks have no matching line.
You help finish the loading and keep the argument from blocking the whole square.
You publicly back the sellers and force the collector to explain each seizure.
You refuse to enter a tax dispute that is not yours.
In a South Blue kingdom, a royal collector loads sacks directly onto a cart bearing the local seal. Three sellers insist they already paid the same levy.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_samba_pa: The band covers the chaos and turns the evacuation into another part of the show.
Play louder
You send half the band to hold the crowd while the rest keep the rhythm.
Split the band
The silence finally makes everyone understand the accident is real.
Stop the music
The float is stopped, but the band arrives behind it with no room to pass. The musicians must either break the parade or improvise around the blockage.
The Band Splits
Nobody understands fast enough and panic spreads ahead of the float.
The crowd turns your command into a coordinated move without stopping the music.
The crowd clears late; several stalls are knocked over.
One clear command opens the lane.
Clear the crowd
You cut the cloth jamming the wheel; the float loses its decoration but regains control.
Cut the banner
The drawbar knocks you down and the float crashes into a row of chairs.
You straighten the float without even breaking the parade rhythm.
You slow the float, but a wheel crushes part of the set.
You put the float back on line before it reaches the crowd.
Steer the float
In Samba City, a parade float loses a steering wheel and drifts toward the stands. The band keeps playing, convinced the swerve is part of the show.
Float Gone Sideways
Four months later, Samba sends you an official invitation to the next parade.
Accept the invitation
You turn the invitation into a paid contract and make your role clear.
Ask for a fee
A Samba City organizer finds your address four months after the accident. The next parade wants to reuse your improvisation instead of hiding it.
Invitation from Samba
You let the musicians take the credit; their piece becomes the memory of the day.
Let the band own it
The new sequence carries your name in the program and the crowd embraces it.
Take credit
Eight months later, the parade repeats the detour born from the accident. This time it is deliberate, and the city wants to know whose name should go on it.
The Improvised Passage
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_seventy_: You refuse to touch the crate and return it to base procedure.
You break the seal before enough witnesses that nobody can rewrite the story afterward.
A handler pays you to look away; the crate moves stacks before inventory.
You have the crate logged as inspection evidence and it leaves the dock under seal.
At the 74th Branch, a quartermaster counts one crate more than the manifest. Two handlers swear it came from a civilian ship and nobody wants to sign for it.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_smoke_ov: You alter course and later find a coastal trader heating tar on its hull. Nothing was burning.
You leave the coast behind and refuse to turn every column of smoke into a detour.
Three signals go toward the smoke. A reply soon comes back: all is well.
A column of smoke rises behind a low South Blue coast. No distress signal accompanies it, but several merchant ships are already altering course to investigate.
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_sorbet_l: You ask for no name to be added to the report. The fix stays the yard’s work.
Refuse credit
Six months later the yard sends its report: the ramp was rebuilt around the flaw you spotted.
Read their report
A Southport courier finds you with a sketch of the repaired ramp. The shipwrights want to know whether they may cite your intervention in their report.
The Yard Report
The yard pays you a small consulting fee and closes the file.
Take the fee
Your name stays attached to the new launch procedure.
Leave the name
A year after the accident, the rebuilt ramp has handled several launches without incident. Southport now settles what it sees as your share of the work.
A Ramp That Holds
The yard loses the tide, but nobody ends up under the hull.
Abort the launch
You release the holding line: the hull hits the water before the ramp gives way.
Cut the holding line
The second wedge finally locks the hull on line.
Drive the second wedge
The first wedge holds, but the hull is still moving. A shipwright points to the second piece under the keel: if it goes, the whole ramp follows.
The Second Wedge
The wedge kicks free and slams your ribs before the hull stops.
You steady the keel without costing the yard its tide window.
You slow the hull, but a support snaps under the load.
You hold long enough for the workers to reset a wedge.
Brace the keel
You clear everyone from the line and let the shipwrights reset the launch.
Clear the ramp
You load the wrong support and two beams split.
You find the alignment fault that was loading the whole ramp sideways.
The hull stays upright, but one wedge cracks under pressure.
You redistribute the support before the hull slides sideways.
Reset the cradle
At Southport, a new hull starts sliding crooked on its ramp as the tide rises. The shipwrights have only minutes before losing their launch window.
Tide Window
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_southpor: You pay market price and the yard prepares the sloop under your name.
Buy the sloop
You walk the sloop, note its repairs, and keep your Berrys.
Inspect the hull
You leave the sloop on its blocks for another buyer.
Walk away
At Southport, a second-hand sloop waits on blocks, hull repaired and price painted on a board. The yard guarantees only that it floats; everything else belongs to the next owner.
Sloop on Blocks
Your people hold the helm steady while the fitting is reset.
Send hands over
You give them a precise mark and let them limp home.
Mark the fault
You take the prototype under tow and turn the trial into a careful return.
Tow it back
The prototype slows abruptly: a rudder fitting has come loose. The shipwrights can repair it afloat, but only if someone stabilizes the situation.
Loose Rudder
You stay outside the trial zone and let the shipwrights learn on their own.
Watch from a distance
The prototype turns sharper than expected and your side takes the hit.
You mirror its turns and give the shipwrights a perfect read of the trial.
You hold pace, but a close crossing damages both hulls.
You stay close enough to flag every flaw.
Match the trial hull
You call the wrong side and the shipwrights reinforce the wrong spot.
You even identify the fitting responsible before the prototype stops.
You spot the twist too late to prevent a fitting from tearing loose.
You spot the twist before it becomes a real break.
Read the hull
A Southport prototype cuts through the swell under a yard flag. Its shipwrights ask you to hold a parallel line: they want to see how the hull behaves in a real ship’s wake.
Trial Hull
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_taya_irr: You protect the crop ready for market and let the seed plot flood.
Save the market crop
You send the remaining flow toward the seed plot. The current harvest suffers, next year survives.
Save the seed field
You open two small breaches and spread the loss between the fields.
Split the damage
The gate finally holds, but the water already released still has to go somewhere. One plot carries next year’s seed; the other holds the crop meant for tomorrow’s market.
The Second Field
The crank breaks and throws you into the channel.
You hold the gate while farmers bring the whole channel back under control.
The gate rises halfway; water still tears through one field edge.
You lift the gate enough to regain control of the flow.
Lift the gate
You open the wrong spillway and send water into an already flooded plot.
You find a diversion that saves both fields.
You limit the damage without saving the first crop.
You divert the overflow into an empty ditch.
Read the flow
You block the lane with empty grain sacks and slow the water.
Build a sack wall
In Taya Village, an irrigation gate jams open after a short rain. Water is already crossing the road and two families are arguing over which plot should be sacrificed first.
The Jammed Gate
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_torino_c: You let the herbalist decide and keep your hands away from a second mistake.
Let the herbalist decide
You sacrifice two handfuls rather than risk a bad remedy.
Discard both
The difference is faint, but enough to discard the wrong leaves.
Compare the scent
At the foot of the tree, two nearly identical bundles have been mixed. Only one can go into the medicine; the other would cause another fever.
The Wrong Leaf
A branch snaps and you fall hard onto a root.
You come down with enough dry leaves for several preparations.
You reach the canopy, but cut yourself on the way.
You gather dry leaves just before the rain.
Climb above the rain
You protect what has already been gathered and leave the climbers to finish.
Cover the baskets
You cut an irritating plant and your hand swells almost immediately.
You also spot the plant masking their scent and speed up the whole harvest.
You find the right patch after losing part of the harvest.
You recognize the useful leaves before they are soaked.
Spot the right vine
In Torino’s canopy, herbalists search for leaves that lose their effect once soaked. Rain is already moving through the branches and a sick patient is waiting in the village.
Leaves Before Rain
event.active_blue_south_blue_01_winter_g: You sacrifice a piece of cargo timber to brace the deck.
Brace with timber
You clear the knots one by one and stop the remaining crates from sliding.
Save the lashings
You lock the deck down until the lashings regain some flexibility.
Wait for the thaw
The wind dies as fast as it came, but the lashings have frozen stiff as wire. A heavy crate is already working its knot loose.
Frozen Lashings
You kill speed and take the cold without trying to make ground.
Kill speed
A sheet lashes the deck and tears your shoulder before it is caught.
Everything is secured before the first real blast hits.
The sail comes down, but a yard strikes the hull during the maneuver.
You shorten sail just before the cold gust hits.
Reef fast
The turn comes too late and the wave lays the ship over.
You put the ship in the one angle where the gust slides instead of slamming.
You take the gust broadside; several lashings fail.
The stern takes the worst of the gust and the deck stays workable.
Put the stern to it
An icy gust drops from South Blue’s cold zone and instantly whitens the rigging. Cargo starts sliding before the rain even turns to sleet.
White Gale
